transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... it's about my eating. See, after my shifts—I'm a cashier over at the supermarket on 5th, which, let me tell you, standing on your feet for eight hours scanning barcodes really does a number on your lower back. My manager, Gary, he won't even let us have those padded mats to stand on. He says they're a tripping hazard, but honestly, I think he's just being cheap. I saw him driving a brand new truck last week, so he's definitely got the money for store supplies. 

But anyway, sorry, after my shift ends, I keep doing this thing where I buy these huge takeout orders. Like, I'll go through the drive-thru and get enough burgers, large fries, a bunch of chicken, and desserts for an entire family. I usually go to the one near the highway because the drive-thru lady there, Brenda, she never forgets my extra BBQ sauce. The other place always forgets it, and if you're paying for it, you should get it, you know? But yeah, I'll just sit there in my car and eat almost all of that food myself before I even drive home.
How often do you find yourself eating large amounts of food in one sitting like this, and do you feel like you can't stop once you start?

How often? Uh, honestly, it's getting to be almost every shift now. Which is five days a week. And it's really ruining the interior of my Honda, by the way. The whole car just smells like stale fry grease and barbecue sauce all the time. I tried hanging one of those little green pine tree air fresheners from the rearview mirror to cover it up, but it just gave me this massive headache. My buddy Craig told me I should sprinkle baking soda all over the floor mats to absorb the smell, but Craig also thinks the earth is flat, so I try not to take his advice too seriously. He's a good guy, though, we played football together back in high school. 

But, um... what were you asking? Oh, right, about stopping. Yeah, I really can't. It's like once I take that first bite, it feels like something inside me just clicks off. Even while I'm sitting there chewing and literally telling myself, Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more, my hands just keep reaching into the bag for the next thing. I just can't seem to make myself quit.
After you finish eating all of that food, how do you usually feel emotionally?

Emotionally? Oh, man. I just feel... terrible. Like, really disgusted with myself. I'll be sitting there in the driver's seat, surrounded by all these wrappers, and the guilt just hits me like a ton of bricks. It's funny, though, speaking of wrappers, you know those little paper cups they put the ketchup in? I don't understand why they can't just make a normal-sized cup. You have to fill up like ten of them just to get enough for a large fry. And then they always get squished in the bag. Last week, I had one explode all over my work pants. The khaki ones. Let me tell you, getting ketchup out of khaki is basically impossible. I tried club soda, I tried that spray stuff you see on TV—the one with the guy who yells all the time? Oxi-something? Didn't work. Now I just have this weird faded pink stain right on the knee. Gary actually wrote me up for being "out of uniform," which is rich coming from a guy who wears the same mustard-stained tie every Tuesday. 

But yeah, after I eat, I just feel so ashamed. Like, why did I just do that again? I just sit there and feel completely worthless.
After you finish eating all of that food, do you ever try to 'make up for it' by doing things like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising a lot more than usual, or skipping meals?

Make up for it? Um, no, not really. I don't make myself throw up or anything. I actually hate throwing up. The last time I threw up was when I had that terrible stomach bug back in, I think it was November? Yeah, right before Thanksgiving. My mom made this chicken noodle soup, but she puts way too much celery in it. I don't know why people even eat celery, it's just crunchy water with strings. You spend more time picking it out of your teeth than actually eating it. I told her, Ma, just use carrots next time, but she never listens. 

But yeah, no, I don't do that. And laxatives? Definitely not. The pharmacy next to our supermarket is always a nightmare anyway. You should see the lines there on a Tuesday, it's ridiculous. The head pharmacist, Diane, she moves at a glacial pace. I swear she's reading every single label like it's a mystery novel. 

And exercising... nah. I mean, I tried to get a gym membership once, at that place with the purple equipment? But they have this loud alarm that goes off if you drop the weights too hard, which just seems really stressful. Like, people are there to work out, let them make a little noise, you know? Plus, after standing at the register all day, my feet are absolutely killing me. I just want to sit down. So, no, I don't do any of that stuff to make up for it. I don't skip meals or anything. I just... I just eat, and then I sit there and feel terrible about it.

Can you describe what it feels like just before you start eating in the car? Do you feel a strong urge or compulsion that you can't resist, or does it feel more like a choice you make even though you know it might not be the best one?

Before I start eating? Um... I don't know, it's hard to explain. It's not really a choice, I guess. It's more like this... this feeling that just takes over. Like I'm on autopilot. You know when you're driving home from work and you suddenly realize you don't remember the last three miles? That happens to me on Interstate 95 all the time. The traffic there is just awful, especially around the exit for the mall. They've been doing construction on that overpass for like, three years now. I don't know what they're actually building, but it seems like there's always just one guy digging a hole while five other guys stand around looking at him. And the orange cones! They're everywhere. I actually ran over one a few months ago. It got wedged right under my bumper, and I had to pull over at a gas station to yank it out. The guy at the pump next to me looked at me like I was crazy. 

But yeah, the urge. It's... it's really strong. I just feel like I *have* to do it, and I can't really fight it. I don't know if that makes sense.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress, or has it affected things like your work, relationships, or daily activities?

Distress? Yeah, I mean... it definitely causes a lot of problems. I still make it to all my shifts at the store, so work is fine. Well, mostly fine, except for Gary breathing down my neck about the uniform policy. But at home... it's really tense. I'm spending money we just don't have on all this food. And the prices at the drive-thrus lately? It's insane. A value meal isn't even a value anymore. I went to get a burger the other day and the total was like, fourteen dollars. For a burger and fries! I remember when you could get a whole meal for five bucks and still have change for a soda. And the sodas are getting smaller, too. They call it a medium, but it looks like a small. I think they just changed the cups to trick people. 

But yeah, the money thing is bad. And I'm keeping it all a secret from my wife. I have to hide the receipts, throw away the bags in the dumpster behind the gas station before I pull into the driveway... it just makes everything at home feel so dishonest. I hate lying to her, but I can't tell her. She wouldn't understand. She's one of those people who can eat half a cookie and just put the rest away. Who does that? You open the package, you eat the cookie. But she just folds the little plastic wrapper over and puts a clip on it. We have a whole drawer full of those chip clips. Half of them are broken anyway. The springs always pop out. 

But yeah, it's really affecting things with my wife. It just feels awful.
Can you recall if there have been times when you felt you couldn't stop eating even though you wanted to?

Yeah... yeah, that happens every time. It's like... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just clicks off. Like a switch. I'll be sitting there, literally telling myself, "Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more," but my hands just keep reaching into the bag for the next thing. It's like my brain and my hands aren't connected anymore. 

Which reminds me of this remote control car I had when I was a kid. You know the ones with the little antenna that always bent in half? I loved that thing. It was bright red, with these big knobby tires. But the remote was so cheap, half the time you'd push the joystick forward and the car would just spin in circles. Or it would pick up a signal from a neighbor's garage door opener and just take off down the street on its own. I chased that car down Elm Street so many times. Old Mr. Henderson used to sit on his porch and just laugh at me. He had this really loud, wheezy laugh, and he always smoked those cheap cigars that smelled like burnt rubber. I don't know how his wife put up with it. She was always out in the garden, planting petunias. She had the best petunias on the block. 

But yeah, it's like that broken remote. I'm telling myself to stop, I want to stop, but I just... I just can't. My hands just keep going until it's all gone.
Can you tell me more about what it feels like when you're eating during these episodes? Specifically, does it feel like you've completely lost control, like you can't stop even if you wanted to?

Yeah, I mean... it's exactly like that. Like I said, it's... once I take that very first bite, it just feels like something in me completely clicks off. Like a switch. And even while I'm sitting there, literally telling myself, "Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more," my hands just keep reaching into the bag for the next thing. It's like I'm watching myself do it but I can't stop it. 

Which is kind of like watching those cooking shows on TV. You know the ones where they have to make a whole meal out of, like, gummy bears and a piece of flank steak? I don't know who comes up with those ingredients. It's always some weird combination. And the judges are always so picky! "Oh, the steak is slightly under-rested." Like, buddy, they had twenty minutes and a microwave, what do you expect? My favorite judge is the guy with the spiky hair, though. He went to all those diners and drive-ins. I actually went to one of the diners he visited once. It was a couple of towns over, and they were famous for this gigantic pancake. It was the size of a hubcap! I tried to eat the whole thing, but I couldn't even make a dent in it. The waitress, Brenda, she was so nice about it. She gave me a box and said nobody ever finishes it. She had this big beehive hairdo, like from the sixties. You don't see those much anymore. It must take a whole can of hairspray just to keep it up there. 

But yeah, the feeling of losing control... it's exactly that. I just can't stop my hands from reaching for more, no matter how much I tell myself to quit.
Can you tell me more about what it feels like when you're eating during these episodes? Specifically, does it feel like you've completely lost control, like you can't stop even if you wanted to?

Yeah, I mean... I feel like I just said this, but yeah, it's exactly like that. I've completely lost control. It's like... the second I take that first bite, something inside my brain just clicks off. I'll literally be sitting there in my car or wherever, thinking to myself, "Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more of this," but my hands just keep reaching into the bag. It's like I'm a passenger in my own body. 

Which is a terrible feeling, being a passenger. I hate riding shotgun. My buddy Greg always insists on driving when we go anywhere, and his car is a disaster. It's an old Honda Civic, and the passenger side window won't roll up all the way, so it always whistles when we get on the highway. And he has this weird smell in his car... kind of like wet dog and old gym socks. He doesn't even have a dog! I told him he needs to buy one of those little pine tree air fresheners, the "Black Ice" ones. Those are the best. They smell like cheap cologne, but it's better than wet dog. I used to buy them in bulk at the auto parts store. The guy who worked there, Sal, he always gave me a discount because we went to high school together. Sal was the starting quarterback our senior year. He threw a touchdown pass in the final seconds of the homecoming game... man, the whole town went crazy. 

But anyway... yeah. Once I start eating, my hands just keep reaching for the next thing, even when I'm telling myself to stop. I just can't stop it.
Do you usually eat this way in secret because you're embarrassed or ashamed of how much you're eating?

Yeah... I mean, absolutely. The shame is just... it's overwhelming. I never do it around anyone else. I'll usually just sit out in my car in the parking lot to eat, or I'll wait until my wife is completely asleep. 

Which, honestly, she sleeps like a rock anyway. We just got one of those memory foam mattresses. You know the ones that come rolled up in a box? I still don't understand how they shrink a whole king-size bed into a box that small. The delivery guy left it out on the porch in the rain, though. The cardboard got all soggy, and I had to drag it up the stairs by myself. My back was killing me for a week. I had to wear this tight brace under my uniform at the store. Being a cashier with a bad back is the worst, because you're just standing on that thin little anti-fatigue mat all day. And half the time, people put heavy stuff like forty-pound bags of dog food or giant cases of water right on the belt instead of leaving it in the cart, so you have to haul it over the scanner. There's this one regular, Mrs. Gable, she buys like ten cases of diet soda every single Tuesday. I don't know who in her house is drinking all that soda. It can't be good for your teeth. 

But anyway, yeah, I hide it all. After she goes to bed and I eat, I take all the empty bags and the wrappers, and I make sure to stuff them and the receipts way, way down deep in the bottom of the kitchen trash. I push it all under the other garbage so she won't ever see how much I actually bought. I just can't let her see that.

And even while I'm sitting there, literally telling myself, "Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more," my hands just keep reaching into the bag for the next thing. It's like I'm watching myself do it but I can't stop it. 

Which is kind of like watching those cooking shows on TV. You know the ones where they have to make a whole meal out of, like, gummy bears and a piece of flank steak? I don't know who comes up with those ingredients. It's always some weird combination. And the judges are always so picky! "Oh, the steak is slightly under-rested." Like, buddy, they had twenty minutes and a microwave, what do you expect? My favorite judge is the guy with the spiky hair, though. He went to all those diners and drive-ins. I actually went to one of the diners he visited once. It was a couple of towns over, and they were famous for this gigantic pancake. It was the size of a hubcap! I tried to eat the whole thing, but I couldn't even make a dent in it. The waitress, Brenda, she was so nice about it. She gave me a box and said nobody ever finishes it. She had this big beehive hairdo, like from the sixties. You don't see those much anymore. It must take a whole can of hairspray just to keep it up there. 

But yeah, the feeling of losing control... it's exactly that. I just can't stop my hands from reaching for more, no matter how much I tell myself to quit.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences eating episodes that feel like they are out of their control, which is a key feature of binge eating disorder and helps differentiate it from other eating disorders.
doctor.question: Can you tell me more about what it feels like when you're eating during these episodes? Specifically, does it feel like you've completely lost control, like you can't stop even if you wanted to?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: Once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me clicks off, and even while I’m telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,' my hands just keep reaching for the next thing.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about the feeling of losing control during eating episodes, which directly matches the Loss_of_Control symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean... I feel like I just said this, but yeah, it's exactly like that. I've completely lost control. It's like... the second I take that first bite, something inside my brain just clicks off. I'll literally be sitting there in my car or wherever, thinking to myself, "Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more of this," but my hands just keep reaching into the bag. It's like I'm a passenger in my own body. 

Which is a terrible feeling, being a passenger. I hate riding shotgun. My buddy Greg always insists on driving when we go anywhere, and his car is a disaster. It's an old Honda Civic, and the passenger side window won't roll up all the way, so it always whistles when we get on the highway. And he has this weird smell in his car... kind of like wet dog and old gym socks. He doesn't even have a dog! I told him he needs to buy one of those little pine tree air fresheners, the "Black Ice" ones. Those are the best. They smell like cheap cologne, but it's better than wet dog. I used to buy them in bulk at the auto parts store. The guy who worked there, Sal, he always gave me a discount because we went to high school together. Sal was the starting quarterback our senior year. He threw a touchdown pass in the final seconds of the homecoming game... man, the whole town went crazy. 

But anyway... yeah. Once I start eating, my hands just keep reaching for the next thing, even when I'm telling myself to stop. I just can't stop it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences eating episodes in secrecy, which would support a diagnosis of binge eating disorder.
doctor.question: Do you usually eat this way in secret because you're embarrassed or ashamed of how much you're eating?

target_item.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
target_item.manifestation: I hide it because I’m ashamed, so I’ll eat in the parking lot or wait until my wife is asleep, then stuff the bags and receipts down in the trash so she won’t see how much I had.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I eat in secret due to embarrassment or shame about the amount I am eating, which directly matches the Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah... I mean, absolutely. The shame is just... it's overwhelming. I never do it around anyone else. I'll usually just sit out in my car in the parking lot to eat, or I'll wait until my wife is completely asleep. 

Which, honestly, she sleeps like a rock anyway. We just got one of those memory foam mattresses. You know the ones that come rolled up in a box? I still don't understand how they shrink a whole king-size bed into a box that small. The delivery guy left it out on the porch in the rain, though. The cardboard got all soggy, and I had to drag it up the stairs by myself. My back was killing me for a week. I had to wear this tight brace under my uniform at the store. Being a cashier with a bad back is the worst, because you're just standing on that thin little anti-fatigue mat all day. And half the time, people put heavy stuff like forty-pound bags of dog food or giant cases of water right on the belt instead of leaving it in the cart, so you have to haul it over the scanner. There's this one regular, Mrs. Gable, she buys like ten cases of diet soda every single Tuesday. I don't know who in her house is drinking all that soda. It can't be good for your teeth. 

But anyway, yeah, I hide it all. After she goes to bed and I eat, I take all the empty bags and the wrappers, and I make sure to stuff them and the receipts way, way down deep in the bottom of the kitchen trash. I push it all under the other garbage so she won't ever see how much I actually bought. I just can't let her see that.
